## A. Builtin coverage

Inventory: `builtins` of the reference. Each `name/arity` runs on eight inputs under `try ... catch "E"`; error wording is the error-probe suite's job.

jq-1.7.1 builtins: 203 match, 4 differ, 0 not implemented, 11 not probed.

| Builtin | Status | Ledger |
|---------|--------|--------|
| `get_jq_origin/0` | differs | host-dependent: Prints the directory of the running binary, so the two tools differ by installation path alone. |
| `strflocaltime/1` | differs | reference-crash: Same jq 1.7.1 assertion abort on a non-string format as strftime/1. |
| `strftime/1` | differs | reference-crash: jq 1.7.1 aborts (`Assertion failed: JVP_HAS_KIND(j, JV_KIND_STRING)`, jv.c:1370) on a non-string format; succinctly reports a catchable error. |
| `strptime/1` | differs | host-dependent: On `"a" | strptime(.)` the weekday of 1900-00-00 is 6 in jq 1.7.1 on macOS, `[…,8,367]` on glibc, and `[…,0,-1]` in succinctly; the value is platform-libc dependent (#5340). |

Not probed: `debug/0` (writes to stderr), `debug/1` (writes to stderr), `env/0` (host environment), `halt/0` (ends the process), `halt_error/0` (ends the process), `halt_error/1` (ends the process), `input/0` (consumes the probe's own input), `inputs/0` (consumes the probe's own input), `now/0` (non-deterministic), `stderr/0` (writes to stderr), `until/2` (does not terminate on the default argument).

## C. Input conformance: JSONTestSuite

Accepting is exit 0. `y_` must be accepted, `n_` rejected, `i_` is implementation-defined. `succinctly` as shipped semi-indexes and validates little; `--validate` is strict RFC 8259.

| y_ | 95 | 95 | 95 | 95 |
| n_ | 188 | 25 | 40 | 0 |
| i_ | 35 | 25 | 31 | 11 |

The ledger lists a case only when `--validate` breaks its `y_`/`n_` expectation or the two tools print different values for an input both accept; jq itself accepts 25 `n_` cases.

## D. Performance (process spawn, ms; matching outputs only)

Median of interleaved repetitions (5 requested, fewer at 100 MB; a row over 15 ms is topped up to 21 where the time allows), CV in parentheses; the tool order rotates each repetition. A speedup is reference ÷ succinctly, so below 1.00x jq is faster, and is a ratio of medians except where marked †: a row that long is moved by run-to-run noise, so its ratio is of each tool's fastest of the 21 runs, which the noise moves least (the times beside it stay medians). A row marked `CV>5%` is noise-dominated, and its ratio is not a finding on its own. `1.8.1 ÷ 1.7.1` is the secondary reference's own change in speed, always of medians.

## E. Memory (peak RSS and private memory, KiB; separate untimed runs, median of 3)

Peak RSS charges a process for the file-backed pages of its mapped executable and libraries, which are shared and reclaimable, so a larger binary reads higher on every row with the same heap (#5578). Private memory leaves them out: on Linux the largest `RssAnon` sampled while the process ran (a lower bound, and coarser for a run of a few milliseconds, so its ratios and the geomean carry the same caveat), on macOS the peak memory footprint. `n/a` where the platform offers neither.

## Reproduce

```bash
cargo build --release --features bench-runner
cargo build --release --features cli,simd,regex,serde --target-dir target/subject
./target/release/succinctly dev compare jq --quick --subject target/subject/release/succinctly --subject-features cli,simd,regex,serde
```
